pr_body:
fix #9956 

Very much work in progress, but wanted to get feedback before going further. Serializing the flags is straightforward as we can add them to the map. 

Deserialization however not so much:

- The bit flags can be of different types (ChunkedArray<T> / CategoricalChunked) hence we would need a common ground or create a temporary representation (e.g. Enum of all bitsettings). I choose the first, but this exposes u8 to the outside.

- Where to implement setting the flags. I choose to not do it on the series directly as not all ChunkedXXX implementations necessarily have flags. This would slightly complicate deserialization as we have to first construct the chunkedarray, alter the bit flags and then call `.into_series`

issue_context.title: Dataframe flags are not preserved by pickling/unpickling
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
>>> import pickle
>>> df1 = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3]}).set_sorted("x"); df1["x"].flags
{'SORTED_ASC': True, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
>>> df2 = pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(df1)); df2["x"].flags
{'SORTED_ASC': False, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
```


### Issue description

When running long-running computations such as data retrieval, I sometimes use caching strategies such as `functools.lru_cache` or `diskcache.Cache` to cache the results with minimum efforts.
Oftentimes these tools use `pickle` for serializing/deserializing, but it seems like this doesn't preserve the flags, and in particular the "SORTED_*" ones.
A typical use case would be something like:

```python
import diskcache

cache = diskcache.Cache(mycachedir)

@cache.memoize(expire=3600)
def get_latest_data(id: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    # do a very slow thing
    return df.set_sorted("time")

def get_analyzed_data(id: str) -> pl.DataFrame:
    data = get_latest_data(id: str)
    # do something using the sorted property of data
    # ERROR
```

I traced this issue back to the pickling/unpickling behaviour I displayed above, but I'm not sure _why_ that happens.
If that's an easy fix that would certainly make my life much easier.
Otherwise I'm guessing I could try and come up with my own parquet-based on-disk caching utility, but that would be a big overhead compared to the example above.
I could also keep doing that I'm doing, always rerunning `.sort("x")` whenever it is needed, but that's making the code very verbose and potentially slower than usual (I do a _lot_ of asof joins!).

### Expected behavior

```python
assert df2["x"].flags == {'SORTED_ASC': False, 'SORTED_DESC': False}
```

### Installed versions

<details>

```
--------Version info---------
Polars:              0.18.7
Index type:          UInt32
Platform:            Windows-10-10.0.19045-SP0
Python:              3.11.2 (tags/v3.11.2:878ead1, Feb  7 2023, 16:38:35) [MSC v.1934 64 bit (AMD64)]

```

</details>
